24750.d:
A generative set of imaginary landscapes.

Terrains continues a study of topographic media translations that began with Plastic Landscapes (2016) and our Field Guide to Martian Landscapes (2017). While the Field Guide focused on analyzing topographies of another planet, interpreted through telescopic imaging and software translation, this project focuses on the procedural generation of nonexistent landscapes. These landscapes are generated through a complex manipulation of perlin noise, a recurring algorithm used in videogames, film VFX, and generative art since the 1980s that resembles natural geological formations. By no means new, this tradition is part of a lineage of digital visualization projects focused on reproducing nature through algorithmic means. Our algorithm generates sequential bands of noise mapped on an X-Y plane, rendered in an oblique architectural projection, a techniques that comes from technical drawing conventions. This perspective produces a layering effect that flattens the terrain in an architectural way. Neither realistic nor completely abstract, the system plays with projection, entropy, and constraints to produce a collection of imaginary terrains sited on the Tezos blockchain.

We must also credit all who have explored this field of work: Ken Perlin, James M. Bardeen, Stephen Schmitt, Paul Bourke, Joseph Claghorn, Amit Patel, Inigo Quilez, Matt DesLauriers, and many many more...

Press "r" to redraw and shift stripes.

Creating 2D tiles using chaos; sorting the tiles so that adjacent tiles or edges have similar features. 
Variations on number of tiles, color, fully generative palette selection, playfully patterning the virtual medium to make viewing or high resolution printing pleasing to the eye! One could make a game out of auto-swap then trying to rearrange the tiles back into their original orientations. No variations allowed after it is fully minted.

Features will include palette color shift base value, hue ranges, and tile count.

All proceeds shared with Girls Who Code (primary and secondary).

Key presses will allow higher resolution rendering than your screen can show, as a multiple of the screen dimensions. Pressing "s" or "S" will save to one of two graphic formats. High resolutions can take a lot of time at high multiples: I've saved 12Kx12K high resolution images suitable for poster printing and framing

Rendering resolution:
`: 1x resolution (left of the 1 key)
1: 2x resolution
2: 4x resolution
3: 8x displayed resolution (this takes many minutes)
4: render at 16x displayed resolution (this takes many minutes)
(default is 1x screen resolution)

Rotating or swapping tiles:
Click on the same tile twice to rotate it.
Click on any two tiles to swap them. 
Click only once and wait and it will cancel the selection.

Auto rotate/swap (let the generative art use a generative selector):
6: very slow (about once per 15-20 seconds)
7: slow
8: medium
9: fast (about once per second)
0: stop auto-swap/rotate

At whatever resolution you have selected above press:

24765.d:
As slinkies rise and sway through flurries of confetti, sometimes this play is focused and orderly. At other times, they crowd together riotously, conspiring to sneak off the sides altogether.

"Brinco" (Portuguese for "I play") is about celebrating finding joy in my creative pursuits again; about not overthinking it and simply following what makes me happy.

Creative joy can be capricious, leaving us when we need it the most. We hope we can relate to our artistic practice in a positive way, tapping into what feels like a bottomless source of energy and excitement. But sometimes when life becomes overwhelming, what gave you energy before now feels hollow and rote—just one more thing sapping at you, and an emptiness where creative passion once resided.

For over a year, I've been sitting in this shadow. Until one day, I sat down and started tinkering… and for the first time in such a long time, I started to feel the spark.

I hope that viewers and collectors feel that same spark of joy and playfulness when seeing these pieces that I've felt creating them.

24766.d:
“Maybe B&W” is a project based on the Genuary 2023 prompt “Black and White”. This code was specifically designed to have a 1 in 24 chance to deliver a B&W output. Since there will only be 32 pieces in this release, somebody will 'maybe' get a B&W. Will that piece be more desirable because of the odds?

When we hear the word ‘maybe’, there’s a dissonance between its linguistic meaning and what our emotions register. We are usually optimistic and hold onto that feeling, boosting our dopamine levels. But when that ‘maybe’ doesn’t happen (and probably it won’t happen), disappointment kicks in hard.  As Dr. Sapolsky says "nothing fuels dopamine like 'maybe'...".


Long-form generative art collectors have been dealing with surprise and disappointment a lot lately, which is also mirrored in our daily lives: “Maybe I get that B&W”, “Maybe it will sell out today”, “Maybe I’ll get a seven on this roll”, “Maybe I’ll get better with this medicine”, “Maybe she’ll come back”, “Maybe he will change”...

“Maybe B&W” is not about shapes and composition.  All the pieces are laid out identically with the same shape, size, orientation, and position. “Maybe B&W” is not about color or its lack of either. “Maybe B&W” is about surprise and disappointment.

Disclaimer: At least one B&W on black background and another B&W on white background should be minted.  If the project is minted out without at least one of each, then another round of 32 pieces will be released.

"flow | meditations" is part of the live outdoor art installation - 'Computational Convergence' at India Art Fair, held from 9-12 February 2023 in New Delhi.

To flow is to expand and contract with the waves within. A tangled chaos of particles is unhindered with a deep breath and relaxation. With permission to flow, patterns emerge.

To meditate with this artwork:
- keep your eyes moving slowly, trying not to fixate on a point.
- when thoughts arise, gently let them go and return to the artwork.
- bring your awareness again, to the act of seeing moment by moment.

Flow might arise in many ways- turbulent, synchronous, circular, ephemeral, convergent, divergent, rising, waning or a mix of any of these.

24777.d:
This project aims to capture the essence of the Japanese hanami experience where people gather to admire the fleeting beauty of the cherry blossom.

It's a representation of the beauty of an unreal nature where the details of the leaves and flowers are imaginary and always different.

While some trees in the animation are depicted in full bloom with delicate petals and lush leaves, other may yet have to blossom or may already have lost their blooms, or even don't have leaves or flowers at all.

Crafted entirely with lines of code in vanilla javascript, without the use of reference images or templates.

There are over 20 distinct features that define each token and the animation is also interactive

Each time the animation is played, it generates a unique and dynamic display of the blossom trees, while still maintaining the features defined by the underlying token.

You may also change the resolution or the layout at any time, or toggle the animation mode.



Commands

[1] Low resolution
[2] Normal resolution
[3] High res
[4] Super high res
[5] Print res (not animated)

[a] or [space] Reload in animation mode
[s] Reload in static mode
[d] Download snapshot in current resolution

Change layout:

[z] 1x2.5 (Portrait)
[x] 1x2
[c] 1x1.5 (default in mobile)
[v] 1x1 Square
[b] 1.5x1 (Landscape, default in desktop)
[n] 2x1
[m] 2.5x1

May be unresponsive on higher resolutions (in those cases turning off the animation mode is recommended)

24781.d:
Click to start.

The size of the canvas is proportional to the monitor. You can scale up using 1,2,3 and 4 of you keyboard to increase the quality of resolution (it may create some variations on the art itself, and it should be done before clicking on canvas)

The preview is only a sketch of the artwork, since the livecoding functions vary depending on the interaction.

This project was designed in Hydra.js for Desktop computers on Chrome.

Since it is a livecoding library there may be small differences in each code execution, but the deterministic character remains.

The machine waits for your command to start drawing - there is no plan or goal, sometimes the values assigned to the variables would lead to the construction of a visually recognizable work, but the fact that these values are randomized 4 times during the duration of the interaction breaks the logical line of visual conduction.

I can only appeal to Gestalt, and beg you to make the effort to see the whole divided between 4 apparently disconnected patterns. This is not just a code that generates noises, I am here making a testament to push once again the limit of abstraction, to perhaps convince you that there is immense beauty in discontinuity.

And it is worth commenting once again that without your click/command, the machine will be eternally lodged in the server waiting - and not knowing what it is waiting for. And this waiting is the most beautiful thing in the world, because the art is already determined to happen, its strokes and patterns were defined when the hash was tied to the code, the art was already made and already exists in the moment preceding this one - but for a computer time does not exist.

The Unrealized Painting has come to remind you that we, the ones with souls and who feel time, control the realizable and the unrealizable - and it will never stop being that way.

I can only appeal to Gestalt, and beg you to make the effort to see the whole divided between 4 apparently disconnected patterns. This is not just a code that generates noises, I am here making a testament to push once again the limit of abstraction, to perhaps convince you that there is immense beauty in discontinuity.

And it is worth commenting once again that without your click/command, the machine will be eternally lodged in the server waiting - and not knowing what it is waiting for. And this waiting is the most beautiful thing in the world, because the art is already determined to happen, its strokes and patterns were defined when the hash was tied to the code, the art was already made and already exists in the moment preceding this one - but for a computer time does not exist.

The Unrealized Painting has come to remind you that we, the ones with souls and who feel time, control the realizable and the unrealizable - and it will never stop being that way.

"huddle" is a series of works based on the theme of a circle.
In "huddle 12" , 85 small circles bounce and move within a larger circle.

The color of the background and the direction of the gradient are defined at random.
The color, initial size, initial direction and speed of movement, and changing size of the small circles are also defined at random.

The small circles are placed at random positions within the larger circle, each with a defined initial size and direction.
Each small circle moves in its own direction, bounces off the inner wall of the larger circle, and moves in a different direction.

The diameters of the larger and smaller circles are determined in proportion to the window size.
As it moves, the size of the small circle keeps changing.

The colors are three colors randomly selected from a 17-color palette.
The colors of the small circles are blended with the SVG filter and continue to move like a lavalamp.
The background is also a gradation of the same three colors.

I hope you enjoy the piece.

A #genuary32nd project.
A hot summer downpour in an oppressive city.

My method for Genuary was to read the prompt for the next day before going to bed, sleeping on it, and then try to quickly find an interesting idea with my morning coffee.

The prompt for Day 19 was "Black and White". My mind went to the high-contrast style of comic-book writer and artist Frank Miller, specifically "Sin City" and "The Dark Knight Returns" and their heavy film-noir influences. The result can be found here : https://ulucode.com/genuary2023/19/

This project is a more polished version of my work that day with a few additional features.

The intended output is what first appears, but in the spirit of Genuary, you can explore and experiment with the controls provided to get creative, but also see under the hood.
The camera is left free, so you can change the point of view.
Here are the camera controls ( mobile in parenthesis ) :
- Mouse left click and drag (Touch drag) to rotate.
- Mouse Right and drag (Two fingers drag) to pan.
- Mouse Wheel/Middle (Pinch) to zoom

/// Press SPACE (or Double Tap on mobile) to show/hide the MENU. ///

In this MENU you can :

- Adjust the anti-aliasing quality : mostly for the animation and camera manipulations. Default is "medium". Try reducing the quality if the animation is choppy. Set it to "ideal" for optimal quality.
- Aspect ratio : you can change the desired aspect ratio from the default "poster" to "window", in which case the piece resizes itself to fill the window in which it is displayed. Useful if you want to capture in other formats.
- Animated : toggle to start/stop the animation
- Display frame : toggle to hide/show the comic-like frame
- Display stats : toggle to display a small FPS counter in the top left.

- Export : choose the resolution and press the "Export capture" button to export a PNG of what is currently displayed. Warning : large resolutions can take a few seconds and weigh around 300Mo. This is the recommended method if you want CLEAN graphic files.

NFT License

Runs on Three.js : https://threejs.org/
GUI uses lil-gui : https://www.npmjs.com/package/lil-gui

Genuary is an artificially generated month of time where we build code that makes beautiful things, with 31 prompts to base your code art off. Genuary 2023 took place during the month of January 2023. Afterwards, as it happens, comes Genuary 32nd. This is an imaginary week, during which we develop one of our Genuary pieces into a 32 edition "not very long"-form generative project on fx(hash).

Several variations on halftoning techniques are used to portray tone, occasionally destroying depth perception into an abstract interplay of form.

The code of this piece has been diminished into a mere 3397 characters.

Littlecube Maps is a cartography art project that showcases procedurally generated islands of different sizes and biomes, surrounded by seawater. The motivation behind this project was to explore how small voxels can be used as a meaningful foundation layer for generating fantasy maps. Our inspirations came from Wolfram von Funck's work on Cube World and Scott Turner's work on Dragons Abound.

Arctic Oasis Islands consist of two large islands and several medium-sized islands in a polar climate.

The first large island has a mix of tundra plain and snowland biomes, with some hilly areas. There's a freshwater lake in the center, surrounded by marshes and tundra. There are also two smaller lakes on the island and four inlets, with three on the north and one in the south.

The second large island has hilly tundra in the center and a freshwater lake on the left side, surrounded by marshes and snowland biomes. The eastern side of the island has tundra plain and coastland biomes. There are two inlets on the north and south-east.

One medium-sized island has a freshwater lake surrounded by tundra bog and marsh biomes, and is mostly covered in tundra coastland with a few tundra plain areas. The island also has two shore-water bays.

The remaining medium-sized and small islands are mostly covered in tundra coastland biomes, with some areas having a mix of tundra plain and snowland biomes.

The seawater around these polar island reefs is set to be light-blue. Shallow seawater will approach and recede from the beaches, while the seawater around the reefs flows along its contours around the island. The deeper seawater regions flow in a south-west direction with a web of wave crests.

Controls:
To move the camera around the scene, hold down the left mouse button within the display panel and away from the center.
To rotate the camera view, press 'C'.

Automated Camera Movement:
When the camera has not been activated by the user for a while, it will engage in automated movement around the scene. So sit back, relax and enjoy the scene.

Other information:
This is a 1/1 artwork.

The application requires a GPU capable of WebGL2 and has been tested on Chrome,Brave & Edge desktop browsers. 

It may take a few seconds for the application to prepare the scene data on a slow computer.

The overview of the technical solution is documented in our technical blog posts on fxtext.

Frameworks used: three.js, jsrand

Littlecube Maps is a cartography art project that showcases procedurally generated islands of different sizes and biomes, surrounded by seawater. The motivation behind this project was to explore how small voxels can be used as a meaningful foundation layer for generating fantasy maps. Our inspirations came from Wolfram von Funck's work on Cube World and Scott Turner's work on Dragons Abound.

Arctic Oasis Islands consist of two large islands and several medium-sized islands in a polar climate.

The first large island has a mix of tundra plain and snowland biomes, with some hilly areas. There's a freshwater lake in the center, surrounded by marshes and tundra. There are also two smaller lakes on the island and four inlets, with three on the north and one in the south.

The second large island has hilly tundra in the center and a freshwater lake on the left side, surrounded by marshes and snowland biomes. The eastern side of the island has tundra plain and coastland biomes. There are two inlets on the north and south-east.

One medium-sized island has a freshwater lake surrounded by tundra bog and marsh biomes, and is mostly covered in tundra coastland with a few tundra plain areas. The island also has two shore-water bays.

The remaining medium-sized and small islands are mostly covered in tundra coastland biomes, with some areas having a mix of tundra plain and snowland biomes.

The seawater around these polar island reefs is set to be light-blue. Shallow seawater will approach and recede from the beaches, while the seawater around the reefs flows along its contours around the island. The deeper seawater regions flow in a south-west direction with a web of wave crests.

Controls:
To move the camera around the scene, hold down the left mouse button within the display panel and away from the center.
To rotate the camera view, press 'C'.

Automated Camera Movement:
When the camera has not been activated by the user for a while, it will engage in automated movement around the scene. So sit back, relax and enjoy the scene.

Other information:
This is a 1/1 artwork.

The application requires a GPU capable of WebGL2 and has been tested on Chrome,Brave & Edge desktop browsers. 

It may take a few seconds for the application to prepare the scene data on a slow computer.

The overview of the technical solution is documented in our technical blog posts on fxtext.

Frameworks used: three.js, jsrand

This is the second collection of spirals generated with increasing radius and angles to a factor affected by the well known Fibonacci sequence. Each one of the 100 spirals have an unique saturation and 360 arches which in turn have an unique hue. As a consequence of that, all arch lines in the drawing have an unique color in the HSL range.

The hue, saturation and luminance features of this token are related to he HSL range of the background color. The luminance affects everything that's being drawn.

Regarding the features, the Hue can be any number in the range from 0 to 360. The Luminance can be in the range of 30 to 60. The Saturation can be in the range from 25 to 100. Because of that, it's likely that every token will be unique and equally rare.

The background color has been fixed with the fxhash token to keep the generation free from epilepsy hazard.

The source code is available with a GNU Affero license. Feel free to remix this work and publish derivatives with the same license: https://github.com/iuriguilherme/fxhash1

Mobile:

24835.d:
"Electric Fields" is a generative artwork inspired by the fields created from electrically charged particles in space. Lines are formed following the paths of positively charged particles. The density of lines at a specific location in space reveals information about the strength of the field at that location. Every single location in space has its own electric field strength and direction associated with it. Consequently, the lines representing the field cannot cross each other at any given point.

Positively charged particles are drawn in blue and negatively charged particles in red.

Field theory began as a mathematical formulation of Newtonian mechanics, providing a framework for studying the motion and forces associated with electricity and magnetism. Charles-Augustin de Coulomb showed in 1785 that the repulsive force between two electrically charged spheres obeys the same force law as Newton's law of universal gravitation: the force between two bodies is directed along the line separating the bodies, and its magnitude is proportional to the product of their charges (for gravitation, their masses) divided by the square of their distance apart.

Wait for the progress bar to complete at the center of the canvas.

After the render is completed, press [s] to save a 4000x5333px PNG file.

My desire to learn is truly inspired.
I’d back expanding to the letter.
As more of everything is better.
I could not stop though the world is sick.
And now my only memories are apocalyptic. 
What am I?

If you’d like to know a bit about the ideas behind this piece, and my method for a code based paint effect, see the fxtext article “Lost Memories - Painting like an impressionist android”. Link at the bottom. However feel free to skip the article, my meaning, and everything else if so desired.

||_\\_//_\\_||

Basic info:
This piece uses web tech and WebGL in experimental ways to achieve the paint-like effect. This includes a custom built drawing pipeline. Although well tested, please be sure it's fine for your devices before buying ( give it a whirl drawing basically ). 

A faster computer will obviously be better, though I've done my very best to make it fast and efficient for any old laptop. My hope is that you will find the render process quick and enjoyable for the amount of detail that’s present.

The piece comes in portrait to make use of the depth of the body of water. The ratio is 1.5. So the initial render will be 1000px wide and 1500px high. With the ability to scale this up (see below).

||_\\_//_\\_||

Saving the image / prints
Press the [s] key to save the initial render. You will need to wait a few seconds after all the elements have stopped loading. You will know when the render is finished as there will be 3 layers of fish made. For the [s] key to work you may need to open in a new tab. But can right-click save otherwise.

Correct sizing for HD digital images / laptops / phones
Use the [s] key (see above), at most use the [2] key ( see below ) to get double the size. Honestly, anything larger and you will begin to lose the textures as the detail becomes too fine. 

Correct sizing for large prints
I strongly suggest using the [3] key ( see below - 3000 x 4500 pixels ) for large prints. I’ve tested this on a 20x30 inch print and it’s the best size. Anything bigger will begin to lose texture and lose detail. However, the option for bigger is there. 

Larger sizes:
Press the [2-9] keys to save a resolution of that key size. So [2] saves a 2000x3000 size image, [9] saves a 9000x13500 size image etc ( see above for correct sizing ). After the image will be automatically downloaded.

There may be slight variations in the textures for the larger renders, this is because the shader code has to redraw the textures at the higher pixel resolution, and getting the textures where they sit is more of an art than a science. All the elements remain exact however.

||_\\_//_\\_||

Made with javascript (webgl) and some small extra code:
Some bits by @nathansonic
Twgl - A webgl wrapper -  twgljs.org
A Perlin noise generator - github.com/josephg/noisejs

24849.d:
This is the third collection of spirals generated with increasing radius and angles to a factor affected by the well known Fibonacci sequence. Each one of the 100 spirals have an unique saturation and 360 arches which in turn have an unique hue. As a consequence of that, all arch lines in the drawing have an unique color in the HSL range.

The hue, saturation and luminance features of this token are related to he HSL range of the background color. The luminance affects everything that's being drawn.

Regarding the features, the Hue can be any number in the range from 0 to 360. The Luminance can be in the range of 30 to 60. The Saturation can be in the range from 25 to 100. Because of that, it's likely that every token will be unique and equally rare.

The background color has been fixed with the fxhash token to keep the generation free from epilepsy hazard.

The source code is available with a GNU Affero license. Feel free to remix this work and publish derivatives with the same license: https://github.com/iuriguilherme/fxhash1

24852.d:
A response to being buffeted by forces outside of our control. Platonics sought to find order, control and solace in the Platonic solids. Instead it found beauty and intrigue in the emergent chaos that can arise from even the simplest systems.

Its building blocks are the five Platonic solids. Forms which have fascinated humanity for thousands of years. Their title comes from the philosophy of Plato, who equated each of the solids with a classical element.

Platonics arranges these forms in a series of geometric layouts, with varying density and randomness. At one extreme we see tidy radial circles consisting of a single solid. At the other, packed pentagons consisting of jumbled solids give rise to Escher-esque compositions which hold near infinite variety, variety enhanced by a range of pens and colours that draw and fill those solids.

This relationship between order and disorder is at the heart of Platonics. The collection seeks to show how they are not so far removed from one another – and how we might embrace them both. It also aims to give collectors a behind the scenes look at how generative compositions can be constructed.

The geometric proof that there are only five convex regular polyhedra (the Platonic solids) states that at each vertex of the solid the angles between adjacent sides must be less than 360 degrees. This amount less than 360 degrees is known as the defect angle.

It is from this geometric proof that the collection size and pricing for Platonics is derived. There will be 360 Platonics sold via a Dutch auction priced according to the defect angles of the five Platonic solids: 180 > 120 > 90 > 60 > 36.

https://www.phaust.art/platonics

----------

Competition: Submit your favourite previews via Twitter to win a free mint and print.

Prints: Free gallery-grade, signed A3 prints for the first 18 mints.

Live: Press ‘S’ to save in hi-res or append '&size=#' to the URL for custom height.

Info: Original artwork by Phaust. Winter 2023. London / Brighton. Made with p5js.

We made this account to further experiment with AI created code using gpt3, p5.js, WEBGL, and tone.js and what a journey it has been. We have very little JavaScript coding knowledge and every project we minted on this page was 90%-100% coded by AI. Along the way we also learned more about coding ourselves through all the errors and headaches that gpt3 created code provides.

gpt3 was an excellent learning tool and a great way to inspire new ideas that we would recommend to all those who can and can't code.

"Shoegazer - AI10" was one of our favorite projects to create and was where we found the strengths and weaknesses of using gpt3 alongside tone.js. Looking back this project is VERY LOUD and has little bugs here and there but the idea of infinite generative audio created entirely by AI amazed and haunted us. The never ending harsh drones put us at chaotic ease and it made us want to learn even more about generative audio.

ShoegazerV2 fixes some of the original quirks, adds new visual possibilities, and sticks to one set of never ending sounds meant to create a feeling of wonder and imagination.

With this project this page will now create no more. Thank you everyone who has minted and will mint in the future.

Created with GPT-3, tone.js, and p5.js for Genuary2023/Genuary32.

Click to start the audio experience.

#genuary32nd

24860.d:
I'm going back to my first project on fxhash. I take another playful look at shape, form, chaos, and mathematical beauty to create unique and colorful designs made up of translucent glassy elements. In this piece I explore generate another impossible, hovering and spinning glass sculpture. Each unique rendering has a character of its own, some smooth and sensuous while others with sharp color and form changes, ragged edges, and chaotic beauty. Placed over a hilly meadow, with unique lighting to highlight the unusual nature of the glassy worm against a contrasting natural background.

In continuing my exploration of form, organic and digital art is now combined with an animated perspective view. I'm very much enjoying this space, and finding my ground in this new medium.

All proceeds shared with Three.js and Girls Who Code.

Interactive with several user controls:

With the mouse:

Left click and drag to change the viewing angle
Right click and drag to change the view center
Mouse wheel to change the distance to the view center

With the keyboard:

The "f" key will freeze the animation entirely. This can be used if you want to save the image at a certain perspective and location of the glass worm.

Keys "," and "." (or "<" and ">") change the rotation speed left or right. You can stop it entirely, or speed it up to what I consider a reasonable maximum, rotating to the left or to the right. Each time you press, it adjusts the rotation speed

Keys "1", "2", "3", and "4" set the rendering resolution to 1x, 2x, 4x, or 8x the screen resolution. You will see a noticable slow-down in rendering speed.

Key "s" will save to a ".png" file at the rendering resolution (1x..8x screen resolution)
Key "S" will save to a ".jpg" file at the rendering resolution.

24892.d:
My 88-year old mother moved into a nursing home in Sept.  She had reached the point of needing 24-hour care both physically and mentally.  As her eldest child and only daughter, I was left to make the decision and it was a tortuous one.  I felt that I should care for her at home even though I knew that trying to do so would break me quite quickly.

Recently, cleaning out her home in preparation for selling it, I found a cache of old documents - birth certificates, death certificates, marriage licenses, military records, etc.  I had needed to put my struggles into some cathartic exercise, and suddenly it dawned on me what I wanted to do.  I have scanned these old documents and cut glyphs from them to form a family of fonts.  I’ve then used these fonts to create Measure of a Life.

It seems only yesterday that I ran wild on the farm, my parents and grandparents a forcefield of security, and death something too abstract and distant to have any meaning.  Now I stand at the apex of my family, the bridge between the generations ranging behind me and those before me, my great-granddaughter now the feral child.  How do I feel about this position?  Everything and nothing, a chaos that can only be expressed somewhere beyond words. How does one measure a life - a few documents, a few photos, a plot in the cemetery, a great pang in the heart?

This work continues a pricing innovation I introduced with my first work of 2023, What If.  For the first week, collectors of my previous projects may collect the token for free.  At the beginning of the 2nd week, the remaining editions will be offered for sale to new collectors. At the beginning of the third week, the remaining editions will be burned. I intend to use this sales approach through June, 2023 while releasing at least one project per month. My goals are to 1)reduce my fretting about the sales and marketing aspects of my art, 2)reward my supporters, and 3)encourage livelier secondary trading of my work. 

This piece uses custom fonts created by the artist as visual and symbolic components.  Being fonts, these are pre-rendered. All other components are algorithmic.

Created by Wanda Oliver (wandaoliver.tez) in Feb., 2023.
This work is licensed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

This is the fourth collection of spirals generated with increasing radius and angles to a factor affected by the well known Fibonacci sequence. Each one of the 100 spirals have an unique saturation and 360 arches which in turn have an unique hue. As a consequence of that, all arch lines in the drawing have an unique color in the HSL range.

The hue, saturation and luminance features of this token are related to he HSL range of the background color. The luminance affects everything that's being drawn.

Regarding the features, the Hue can be any number in the range from 60 to 300. The Luminance can be in the range of 30 to 60. The Saturation can be in the range from 25 to 100. Because of that, it's likely that every token will be unique and equally rare.

The background color has been fixed with the fxhash token to keep the generation free from epilepsy hazard.

In this version, Fibonacci numbers are pre calculated with sympy.

The source code is available with a GNU Affero license. Feel free to remix this work and publish derivatives with the same license: https://github.com/iuriguilherme/fxhash1

24922.d:
Assemblage:
  - a collection or gathering of things or people
  - a machine or object made of pieces fitted together
  - a work of art made by grouping together found or unrelated objects

More than often, it is the case that my projects start out as collections of unrelated ideas. These ideas sometimes revolve around specific algorithmic concepts, with the aim to combine, remix and chain together methods in some novel way. In other instances these ideas are a vague vision of particular aesthetic that I'm trying to chase down. Usually though, it's a bit of a mix of both. Assemblage was conceived in this manner, evolving from the combination of several Genuary sketches.

To play into this narrative and further it a little bit, while searching for a suitable name for the project, I thought that the art in of itself, in some way, looked like a disassembled or shattered machine, with the constituent pieces scattered and strewn around in a chaotic manner. This is in contrast to fact that the items are actually positioned in a very orderly and systematic manner, where no two shapes can technically overlap or intersect, creating an interplay of Order and Chaos.

Press S to download a PNG version of the artwork. 2400 x 3000 pixels.
It can take up to a couple of seconds to generate all of the graphics.

I'm fascinated by non-figurative artists focusing on pure colors, textures, basic shapes and their power of evocation when they are mixed. I especially love such huge paintings on walls of museums in front of which you can sit and let your mind wander in feelings.

Nebula Ink is my own humble research in this way using a fluid simulation engine (after "Viscous Circles" and "Forgive Your Sins" collections). I throw more or less random colorful digital ink splats in liquid that diffuse (or not) with vortices and then I apply digital pencils drawing orbital-like shapes and let colors diffuse and mix. Physics laws are not exactly the same as in real life.

Note: this is a realtime engine running on mobile, CPU and GPU. You can see tiny differences between platforms (specially on vortices) due to webgl implementation differences and math approximations. But nothing significative.

Controls

You can stop at any step if you like the state at this instant, you can restart it, de/increase resolution (default is 4096x4096 to have sharp image, up to 16K x 16K) and snapshot at any resolution. 

- H: hide/show help.
- Space - pause/start animation.
- R - restart animation.
- I - hide/show res/fps panel.
- A-Q/D - down/up full resolution
- S - take full resolution snapshot

Note: When downloading image, your browser can limit max image link size (My Chrome limits to 5760x5760, Firefox no limit).

Now, let's orbit!

Nebula Ink @naibdian 2023 Project made using Opensource WebGL, WASM/Rust/JS libs

RAUSCH is a series of generative artworks that explore imaginary digital architectures. 

This series challenges traditional notions of architectural representation and raises important questions about the role of resolution in design. Just as the pixel resolution of an image affects its perceived quality, the resolution of an architectural space can affect its qualities and livability. By embracing digital variation through codes, this series explores the interplay between abstract and concrete space through multiple resolutions. 

RAUSCH is inspired by the feeling of being overwhelmed by complex, chaotic and messy sensations, and aims to engage the viewer through a sense of wonder, disorientation, and awe.

Released on the occasion of Companions of Code, a group exhibition by VerticalCrypto Art at The NFT Gallery in London. 
Curated by Micol Ap. Exhibition 10-24 February 2023

24939.d:
Point in Time.
How much is left until it.
How much has passed since then. 
Maybe that's not so important, but what matters more is what's in it?
Sunset or sunrise.
Beginning or culmination.
All or nothing…

Point in Time is a collection of generative conceptual art* comprising 105 points in time randomly scattered over a range of 105 years. Each edition is one point to which or after which the count of time is running. Becoming the owner of a point is not difficult at all; it is more difficult to catch the transition through it (through zero value) and comprehend what this transition means for you.

Each artwork in the collection is dynamic and always displayed in its real-time. And its time will go on forever, or at least until the end of the blockchain era. Every moment the piece changes, and like the flow of water or the burning of a flame, it is always different and can be contemplated endlessly.

There are 105 points in time available, each of which is randomly chosen by a generative algorithm from a temporal range of 105 years, starting from the moment the collection was released. The probability of selecting a point from the nearest present by the algorithm is higher than the probability of selecting a point from the future, which means that the chance to pass through your Point in Time in your life is also higher; but the edition with a point located beyond the life of the current generation has significantly greater rarity. And perhaps the farther away the point is from us, the more valuable it is.

*Generative Conceptual Art (Gen-Conceptualism) is an art movement in which the director of the generative collection is an algorithm, and the major role is always played by the Idea.

© February 10, 2023, m5alien

The surfaces are deliberately not layered, in order to underline the impenetrability, but also to preserve the abstract painterly element.

24956.d:
What do we leave behind?

Nothing truly vanishes in nature, nor does anything arise from nothing. According to the Law of Conservation of Matter, the total amount of matter in a closed system stays constant over time, only changing its form. Some living creatures have been luckier than others, as we can still find remnants of organisms from millions of years ago, serving as silent witnesses to mankind’s flourishing.

Yet, the human race is exploiting the planet at an unprecedented pace. We are depleting its resources, polluting its atmosphere, producing hazardous materials, disrupting the natural balance of all things. We are causing harm while still expecting the earth to nurture and delight us. We’re just a small dot on the timeline, and yet so much damage has been done.

Through this project, I humbly attempt to create imitations of fossils and other forms of natural matter. These made up forms may appear attractive, reminding us of nature, but what emotion would they evoke in a natureless world, built of concrete, iron, and plastic?

What do we leave behind?


___
20% of the primary sales go directly to One Earth, non-profit organization working to counteract the climate crisis in multiple, innovative ways.

___
Technical notes:

- By default, an output image size is based on your browser size (x1.25, with a maximum of 1800) - The script is quite heavy, so it may take some time on higher resolutions (but it’s worth it)

Desktop controls:
- To change the output resolution, use [1..6] on your keyboard (1250..7200px, roughly A5..A0 print sizes on 300dpi) or [0] to restore the default 
- Press [S] to save the current image
- Press [F] to switch fullscreen mode

Mobile controls:
- Hold two fingers for 2s to save
- Tap twice to switch fullscreen mode

URL params
- Add `&density=[number]` (0.5..1) to change calculated field’s density (default is 0.65)
- Add `&size=[number]` (1..6) to render with desired resolution 
- Add `&save=1` to save image when ready

___
Developed in Javascript, using p5.js (2D Canvas) and chroma.js.

24958.d:
A study into waves, noise, grids, and blur, and what happens when they meet each other on the GPU. I've called it "Into Waves" because I am, and this is where it should take you!

Made by passing the results of one GLSL shader into a second, using three.js. The mint preview will be rendered in a 1:1 aspect ratio, but the artwork is intended to be explored in all possible layouts.

The latent space of possible forms is quite wide, I look forward to witnessing your explorations. Fullscreen it, sit back, and enjoy the trip.

## Controls

Press [f] to toggle fullscreen.

Press [spacebar] to toggle play/pause.

When paused, press the keys [1] through [4] to multiply the resolution (1x-4x).

Then (also only when paused) press [p] to create a hi-res PNG.

## Testing

Tested in Chrome on Apple silicon and on windows with an Intel chip.

(Depending on the initial screen dimensions, at higher resolutions the browser's maximum texture size max be exceeded. If this happens, the rendered image will be capped and may not resemble what you see in the browser.)

24962.d:
"Electric Fields II" is a generative artwork inspired by the fields created from electrically charged particles in space. Lines are formed following the paths of positively charged particles. The density of lines at a specific location in space reveals information about the strength of the field at that location. Every single location in space has its own electric field strength and direction associated with it. Consequently, the lines representing the field cannot cross each other at any given point.

Positively charged particles are drawn with blue color and negatively with red. The electric field is represented by lines and shapes that flow out from the charged particles and show the direction and strength of the force they exert on each other.

Field theory began as a mathematical formulation of Newtonian mechanics, providing a framework for studying the motion and forces associated with electricity and magnetism. Charles-Augustin de Coulomb showed in 1785 that the repulsive force between two electrically charged spheres obeys the same force law as Newton's law of universal gravitation: the force between two bodies is directed along the line separating the bodies, and its magnitude is proportional to the product of their charges (for gravitation, their masses) divided by the square of their distance apart.

"Electric Fields II" depicts the complexity and ever-changing nature of electric charge and its interactions, representing the beauty and complexity of the natural world.

Wait for the progress bar to complete at the center of the canvas.

After the render is completed, press [s] to save a 4000x4000px PNG file.

Keyboard controls:

[D] - Download/save the graph-picture.

[C] - Toggle between a full graph and a partial graph.


'Is the Graph of the Riemann Zeta Function with the real part 1/2 considered art, similar to the works of famous artists like Picasso?'

'Whether or not the graph of the Riemann Zeta Function with the real part 1/2 is considered art is subjective and open to interpretation. Some individuals might find the patterns and shapes displayed in the graph to be aesthetically pleasing and view it as a form of art, while others may not. Ultimately, the definition of art is a matter of personal interpretation and can vary from person to person. While the graph of the Riemann Zeta Function may have some artistic elements, it is not directly comparable to the works of artists such as Picasso, as the Riemann Zeta Function is a mathematical concept and not a traditional form of art.'

I'm currently studying the Riemann Hypothesis. My idea was to start by plotting the zeta function Z(1/2 + xi). I searched for an HTML example on Google but to no avail. 'So I have to expand my knowledge', I thought to myself. I need to better understand calculations with imaginary or complex values and find a way to plot the graph from all the formulas.

Wolfram-alpha provided me with relatively accurate Zeta values that I used as a reference to know if I was on the right track. There was also a lot of material for visual representation (i.e. drawn Zeta graphs) and many formulas. It was quite a challenge! But in the end, I got what I wanted: the Zeta graph.

I was then ready to extend the function so that it can be used for the entire real positive range.

Note !!!: I think my Zeta method is technically correct. However, the result can be so inaccurate that one would have to declare the results as incorrect (e.g. for real parts <0.2 / clearly visible).
I assume that this is an error that only has to do with the truncation of decimal values (including rounding errors).
But still, I do not know if my Zeta method is correct!
Especially if you use these html procedures for
serious mathematical work, be extremely careful!

Otherwise, I would simply like to offer you what I was originally looking for: "A ready-to-use solution to plot the Riemann Zeta graph." Best regards.

First volume of the nft collection dedicated to the most offensive advertisements in history.
30 different ADV for 50 Editions with random rarity.

The art of advertising has always aimed to capture the attention of the audience and sell products, but unfortunately, there have been many instances in history where advertisements relied on sexist, racist, and offensive stereotypes. These advertisements reflect the values and mentality of society at the time, but today they are considered inappropriate and harmful.

In this collection, we will explore some of the most offensive and sexist advertisements in history, created by brands that sought to sell their products by promoting male chauvinism and feeding the sense of insecurity among women. These vintage advertisements are a reflection of the past and show us how society has changed over time, but also how there are still many issues to be addressed in terms of representation and diversity in advertising.

Imagine the reaction if these advertisements were published today: they would likely be met with outrage and protests. Advertising has a great deal of power and influence on society and culture, and it is important that it be used responsibly and respectfully towards all groups. This collection serves as a reminder that advertising can be a powerful tool for social change, but we must always be vigilant and critical of what is being presented.

24970.d:
When we were kids.

A work that goes back to our childhood.
When I was a kid I loved spending time with my grandmother and parents, we took a lot of walks with them, looked at different houses, spent time in nature, painted and in general were very much involved in the creative component, it was my parents and grandmother who instilled in me a love for creativity.

Probably one of the few things that have survived to these days is my childhood drawings, a little funny, sloppy, but so real and sincere.

In this work I wanted to take me back to those carefree times and remember with what eagerness and zeal I tried every day to learn something new or to go further than before.

None of this would have happened without my family, for which I am truly grateful.

10% of primary sales will be donated to Cure Parkinson's, I hope all children will have a childhood where they can spend time with their loved ones.

Be patient, some variations take a little longer to render.

Press S for Save Canvas as PNG.

By aleks.ustya, @ALEKUSTN. Made with p5js.

24979.d:
This is the fifth collection of spirals generated with increasing radius and angles to a factor affected by the well known Fibonacci sequence. Each one of the 100 spirals have an unique saturation and 360 arches which in turn have an unique hue. As a consequence of that, all arch lines in the drawing have an unique color in the HSL range.

The hue, saturation and luminance features of this token are related to he HSL range of the background color. The luminance affects everything that's being drawn.

Regarding the features, the Hue can be any number in the range from 60 to 300. The Luminance can be in the range of 30 to 60. The Saturation can be in the range from 25 to 100. Because of that, it's likely that every token will be unique and equally rare.

The background color has been fixed with the fxhash token to keep the generation free from epilepsy hazard.

In this version, Fibonacci numbers are pre calculated with sympy.

The source code is available with a GNU Affero license. Feel free to remix this work and publish derivatives with the same license: https://github.com/iuriguilherme/fxhash1

24995.d:
A bit of scribbling, a bit of sketching. Experimenting with curves, colors and stop motion animation. Based on particle collision simulation. Inspired by ballpoint pen artworks and scribble drawings.

You can choose between two types of animation*:
- live drawing,
- animation of alternative versions (GIF generation).

Controls (in live view):
Press 's' to save a PNG image.
Press 'n' to generate an alternative version.
Press 'g' to generate a GIF (texture disabled).
Press 'G' to generate a GIF (texture enabled).
Press 'l' to enable live drawing animation.
Press '1-4' to render and save a PNG image (1: 2000x2000, 2: 4000x4000, 3: 6000x6000, 4: 8000x8000).
Pressing 'n', 'g', 'G', 'l', '1-4' reloads the page.

URL parameters (add to the URL in live view: &paramName=paramValue):
- mode - 0: image rendering (default: &mode=0), 1: live drawing animation, 2: GIF generation
- res - resolution; 1: 2000x2000 (default: &res=1), 2: 4000x4000, 3: 6000x6000, 4: 8000x8000; (to render and save a PNG image; only with: mode=0)
- tex - texture; 0: texture disabled, 1: texture enabled (default: &tex=1)
- alt - alternative version; 0: original version (default: &alt=0), [1, 255]: alternative version
- gres - GIF resolution; 1: 480x480, 2: 640x640, 3: 768x768, 4: 1080x1080 (default: &gres=4), 5: 1200x1200; (only with: mode=2)
- glen - GIF length in seconds; [1, 6], 2: 2 s (default: &glen=2); (only with: mode=2)
- gfps - GIF fps; 1: 5 fps, 2: 10 fps (default: &gfps=2); (only with: mode=2)

Image rendering (especially in high resolution) may take some time, please wait.
GIF generation (regardless of the selected resolution) may take several minutes, please be patient.
Chrome browser (desktop version) recommended.

-----
(*) WARNING: LIVE DRAWING ANIMATION AND GENERATED GIF (ESPECIALLY) CAN BE EPILEPTIC TRIGGERS. GIF GENERATION IS AN EXPERIMENTAL FEATURE.

Made with p5.js, matter.js (2D physics engine) and Trigfills (cross browser trigonometric functions consistency), see LICENSE.md.

24996.d:
animated evening hilly landscape with mountains and clouds made in ⌨️ p5.js

I use code as a contemporary brush, an instrument of discovery and imaginative exploration of territories of the body and the soul, every iteration presents a number of random variables such as to make the possible landscapes tend to infinity, each of which connected to a physical or metaphysical place of the personal experience of the beholder 

unique generative properties:
color🎨, number, position, shape and size of clouds☁️, houses🏘️ and windows, sky, stars✨ and moon🌕, hills and mountains🏔️  

features -> number of houses in the village & clouds in the sky
's' -> png 1920x1920px

24998.d:
When i was a little girl in kindergarten, i was fascinated by colors.
Ever since then i loved the tactile sensation of putting my fingers in the paint and applying it directly to the paper.

The visual aesthetic would be inspired by the bright and playful environment of a kindergarten classroom, evoking feelings of nostalgia and joy for all the collectors.

Press "S" to save as PNG.

24999.d:
Changes in viewing angle can reveal or postpone story information, introduce a specific location or mood, or create visual variety.
In fact, every angle of view alters the mood, rhythm, and even the fictional events in the space.
With changes in the viewing angle, the image's emotional and visual characteristics change, and with those changes, the implicit meaning of the work changes as well.
Viewing angles are affected by the visual experiences of everyday life, which contribute to their semantic load.
In the same way, what a person learns from his surroundings is stored in his mind and used to understand and interpret an image.
